newsitem.title: GREECE: GREEK BANKS TO FACE MERGERS, ACQUISTIONS - BANKER.
newsitem.headline: GREEK BANKS TO FACE MERGERS, ACQUISTIONS - BANKER.

text.p: Mergers and acquisitions will be inevitable for Greece's banking sector as the country moves closer to the EMU, Nickos Nanopoulos, the managing director of private Eurobank, told the Economist conference on Wednesday.
The new competitive conditions in the banking sector warrant larger bank size and the exploitation of synergies such as those from cross-selling, said Nanopoulos.
Concentration with exploitation of economies of scale and lower operating costs, privatisation and specialisation within banking groups are the three prevalent trends, he said.

The EMU and the introduction of the euro present banks with new challenges and the opportunity to expand their product range and geographic horizons, said the managing director of Greece's third largest private bank.

Eurobank which belongs to the European Financial Group held by the Latsis family reached an agreement recently with Credit Lyonnais Grece to buy the latter's retail network. It bought 95 percent of private Interbank in 1996. --Dimitris Kontogiannis, Athens Newsroom +301 3311812-4
